## Problem Statement

Modify the `Date` class so it uses constructors, including an overloaded constructor path for initializing a date with supplied values.

<!-- Slide 36 -->

---

## Date2.cpp

```{.cpp}
#include <iostream>
using namespace std;

class Date {
private:
    int mo;
    int day;
    int year;
public:
    Date(int = 1, int = 1, int = 1);
    void PrintDate();
};

Date::Date(int m, int d, int y) {
    mo = m;
    day = d;
    year = y;
    if (mo > 12) mo = 99;
}

void Date::PrintDate() {
    cout << mo << "/" << day << "/" << year << endl;
}

int main() {
    Date date1, date2(10,15,2009);
    Date date3(21,25,2017);
    date1.PrintDate();
    date2.PrintDate();
    date3.PrintDate();
}
```

## Expected Output
